# support-requests #210: sdas8051 truncates constants above 0xffffff in inline assembly to 24 bits

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/support-requests/210/
- Category: [Fixes that need a decision](../../fix-decision.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17193
- Recommended action: Confirm the decision of bug #4070, apply its patch, and close. The second issue is a question, and Finding has the answer.
- Patch: [bugs-4070.patch](../../patches/bugs-4070.patch), commit [`62b418e14`](https://github.com/mdmower/sdcc/commit/62b418e1478ea1b42f782019b10b5f9509e80a74). Applies to r17193 without the other patches.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The ticket has two issues. The first is a defect in sdas8051, and the second is a question.

In the first issue, inline assembly computes a timer reload value from the constant 125000000.
r17193 assembles the two immediate operands to `74 B7` and `34 F3`, which are the bytes in the
ticket. The value 0x3491 that the reporter expects needs `74 91` and `34 34`. The reporter's code
was compiled for mcs51 with `push acc` and `pop acc`, because sdas8051 does not have `push a`, as
the first comment says. The suffix `UL` that the first comment suggests does not help. The
preprocessor expands the macro in the `__asm` block, and sdas8051 rejects `125000000UL` with
error `q`.

The second issue asks why a program with inline assembly needs
`sdcc_atomic_exchange_rollback_start`, and whether that can be disabled. Interrupt routines that
have inline assembly, or that call a function which the compiler has not analyzed, end with
`ljmp sdcc_atomic_maybe_rollback` in place of `reti`. `checkRestartAtomic` in
`src/SDCCopt.c` selects these routines, and `genEndFunction` in `src/mcs51/gen.c` emits the jump.
The library routine compares the return address with the labels
`sdcc_atomic_exchange_rollback_start` and `sdcc_atomic_exchange_rollback_end`, which
`mcs51_genAtomicSupport` in `src/mcs51/main.c` writes after the interrupt vector table when the
compiler compiles `main`.

A program whose `main` sdcc compiles links, with and without a prototype of the interrupt routine
in the file of `main`. The first comment suggests that this file lacks the prototype, and the
result shows that this does not explain the reporter's message. The reporter's project has its
own `crtstart.asm`, and the ticket does not say how the project gets `main` and the vector table.
With the option `--norestartseqatomics`, which was added for feature request #1015 after this
ticket, the compiler omits the labels. Related has a defect of that option.

## Cause

`minit` in `sdas/as8051/i51mch.c` calls `exprmasks(3)`, and `rngchk` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asexpr.c`
then truncates every constant to 24 bits. 125000000 is 0x7735940 and becomes 0x735940, which is
7559488. `0x10000 - 7559488 / 12 / 200 + 4` is 0xF3B7. Bug #4070 reports this cause for the
address of an `__sfr32`.

## Fix

The patch for bug #4070 fixes the first issue. `minit` calls `exprmasks(4)` and then sets
`a_bytes` to 3, so expression values have 32 bits and the object file keeps 3 address bytes. This
ticket does not need another change.

## Decision

The patch for bug #4070 keeps the object format, and it changes the results of other expressions
whose values do not fit in 24 bits as signed numbers. In the last comment of that ticket a
maintainer prefers the design of upstream asxxxx. The entry for bug #4070 describes the choice.

## Verification

With the patches of this report on r17193, sdas8051 assembles the two operands of the reporter's
code to `74 91` and `34 34`. sdas8051 built from these sources with `exprmasks(3)` restored in
`minit` gives `74 B7` and `34 F3`. Of ten more expressions with constants up to 4000000000,
r17193 gives a wrong byte for four and error `z` for two, and with the patches every byte is
correct. The patches do not have a regression test with a constant above 0xffffff in inline
assembly. `support/regression/tests/bug-4070.c`, the test of the patch, reads and writes
`__sfr32` objects.

For the second issue, a program with an interrupt routine that has inline assembly was linked for
mcs51 on r17193 and with the patches, with and without the prototype in the file of `main`. Every
link succeeds.

## Related

- With `--norestartseqatomics`, the compiler omits the two labels, and interrupt routines of the
  kind under Finding keep `ljmp sdcc_atomic_maybe_rollback`. The linker reports "Undefined Global"
  for both labels, and the link fails. This was reproduced on r17193 and with the patches for an
  interrupt routine that has inline assembly, and with the patches for one that calls a function
  of another file. It is not fixed, because two changes are defensible. If `genEndFunction` emits
  `reti` when the option is given, a program loses the rollback without a message when the file of
  the interrupt routine is compiled with the option and the file of `main` is not. If the compiler
  writes both labels at one address when the option is given, the program links, and the
  interrupt routine keeps the jump to the library routine. `genEndFunction` in `src/ds390/gen.c`
  emits the jump under the condition that mcs51 has.
- Bug #3527 reports the 24-bit evaluation of constants for a pdk assembler.
